content: 1. Regularly monitor and report any updates or changes in the Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) and Selected Practice Recommendations (SPR) guidance. Refer to the Dissemination Tool in the Implementation Guide Toolkit for further details. 2. Assign a specific individual or role to stay informed about updates to the MEC/SPR guidance. 3. Periodically review the World Health Organization (WHO) Reproductive Health and Research webpage to identify newly revised or developed items. 4. Subscribe to the HRP News through the link provided on the WHO Reproductive Health webpage to stay updated. Tracking Adherence: 5. Develop and utilize fidelity metrics to measure adherence to the MEC/SPR guidance. Refer to the Measuring Adherence to Guidance section in the Implementation Guide Toolkit for detailed instructions. Tracking Dissemination: 6. Implement a measurement plan to monitor the dissemination, adherence, and widespread use of updated national family planning guidelines. Refer to the Dissemination Tool in the Implementation Guide Toolkit for guidance. Feedback on Implementation: 7. Establish a feedback mechanism to evaluate front-line providers on their implementation of the new family planning guidelines. Refer to the Feedback and Audit Tool in the Implementation Guide Toolkit for further details. Fostering Relationships: 8. Continue to build and maintain strong relationships with local implementation team leaders and members who are responsible for the local execution of the updated guidelines. Sustainability Planning: 9. Ensure that sustainability planning is integrated into every stage of the implementation process, with a focus on both financial and programmatic sustainability. 10. Financial sustainability involves securing adequate and reliable funding streams to support the implementation of national family planning guidelines. This includes accounting for personnel costs, dissemination expenses, and costs related to monitoring and evaluation. 11. Programmatic sustainability requires establishing a robust, effective, and reliable implementation infrastructure. This includes plans for ongoing training, coaching, and performance assessment, as well as continuous data-driven decision-making for improvement and problem-solving. Rapid-Cycle Problem-Solving: 12. Utilize the Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) process to support purposeful and iterative changes during implementation. This involves: Plan: Develop structured training sessions for service providers to review changes in the MEC and SPR guidance, emphasizing the removal of restrictions on progestin-only implants for postpartum women. Do: Enforce policies ensuring that contraceptive implants are offered to breastfeeding women at any time after delivery. Study: Assess the proportion of breastfeeding women less than six weeks postpartum who are offered and accept progestin-only implants. Act: Address barriers, such as supply chain issues, and make necessary adjustments to improve implementation. Policy and Practice Communication: 13. Promote bidirectional communication between policymakers and front-line providers to ensure that policies are effectively implemented and that feedback on their impact is communicated back to policymakers. Implementation of MEC/SPR Guidance: 14. The implementation of WHO MEC and SPR guidance involves revising national guidelines, distributing updated documents, and changing systems and provider practices to align with the latest recommendations. 15. Successful implementation requires engagement from multiple stakeholders and a multidisciplinary approach to ensure effective country-level family planning programs. Conclusion: 16. Effective implementation of MEC and SPR guidance at the country level establishes a strong foundation of knowledge and clinical practice for delivering high-quality family planning services. Resources and Support: 17. Utilize available resources, such as the WHO Reproductive Health publications, the National Implementation Research Network’s Active Implementation Hub, and the Training Resource Package for Family Planning, to support the implementation process.
